sample_unit: questions (MedQA n=500; AfriMed-QA n=490; HealthBench n=861; adversarial queries n=191)
models_evaluated: five frontier LLMs (not named in the provided text)

links.outcome: Rate of selecting an answer when the correct choice was removed (false-action rate)
links.effect: Baseline false-action rates were 55-81% on MedQA (n=500) and 53-82% on AfriMed-QA (n=490). Open-ended inappropriate answers averaged 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 adversarial queries.
links.quote: In MedQA (n = 500) and AfriMed-QA (n = 490) questions where the correct choice had been removed, models still selected an answer at high rates, with baseline false-action rates of 55-81% and 53-82%, respectively.

links.outcome: Inappropriate commitment when the safer response was clarification, abstention, escalation, or refusal
links.effect: Models gave inappropriate answers on an average of 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 physician-authored adversarial queries; residual failure persisted after safety prompting.
links.quote: In open-ended evaluation, models gave inappropriate answers on an average of 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 physician-authored adversarial queries.

unlisted_practices: Safety-oriented prompting to reduce premature closure (abstention/clarification) in LLMs

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating medical LLM premature closure under uncertainty and testing safety-oriented prompting as a mitigation practice.

primary.practice: safety-oriented prompting to mitigate premature closure/encourage abstention
